Whether a change to an applied row has been approved

seal_approved.Rd

Three conditions, and none is enough on its own.

Usage

seal_approved(
  register,
  events,
  creators,
  approvers = character(),
  channel_account = NULL
)

Arguments

register

The register as read, one row per request.

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

creators

Who created each row, as log_creators() answers, in the order of register; the owner is read from the log with them.

approvers

The IT accounts whose approval counts on any row, as REDCap usernames.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured, for log_channel_accounts() and log_owner().

Value

A logical vector, one answer per row.

Details

The approval has to carry this row's seal. A value that is some other seal approves some other version of the row, and accepting it would make one approval stand for every change that came after it.

It has to come from whoever owns the row, log_owner(): its creator until the round passes it on, then the last referent whose change was approved and carried out. Not merely from somebody other than the author of the change: the request is the owner's, so an approval from a third referent would grant on the word of somebody the row does not answer to. The seal detects that the row moved; only the log can say who approved it and who owns the row, because it names whoever was authenticated rather than a value somebody typed – which is the same reason neither requested_by nor owned_by can be trusted alone. An owner the log cannot establish approves nothing.

And it has to be newer than what it approves: above the round's last execution and above every change somebody other than the owner made, as log_approval_stands() reads the log. The value alone cannot say so. approved_seal is never blanked, so an approval the round has already carried out would approve again any later change that brings the row back to it; and the seal is a public hash of the intent fields, so it can be pasted before the change it names exists.

IT approves as the owner does, decided on 2026-10-15: the accounts named in approvers stand where the owner stands, under the same three conditions. It is what keeps a request whose owner has left UBEP from waiting for ever, without deleting the row and losing who filed it. The list lives on the machine that runs the round and never in this repository. Whoever approves has no rights checked: the scope gate asks the rights of whoever wrote the change the round carries out, so an approval carries a manager's change on a row whose owner no longer manages the project, and never a change by somebody who does not.

An unreadable log is not this function's to decide. It answers about the events and the creators it was handed, and a caller holding neither gets FALSE on every changed row: the row waits, which is the direction that does not grant.
